### 🟡 Changes recommended Registering the server context also changes outbound HTTP span parenting when an application child span is active.
1 open issue - [Preserve active child span parenting for Ratpack outbound HTTP](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20693#discussion_r4308732686) · New
What changed in this PR Preserves Ratpack exception reporting when no handler span starts, independently of exception signal selection. **Changes:** - Registers the request context when controller telemetry is disabled. - Adds error-attribution coverage for synchronous, blocking, asynchronous, and forked execution. - Wires disabled-controller test variants for both supported test suites. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | instrumentation/​ratpack/​ratpack-1.4/​javaagent/​src/​main/​java/​io/​opentelemetry/​javaagent/​instrumentation/​ratpack/​v1_4/​TracingHandler.java | Registers context without a handler span. | | instrumentation/​ratpack/​ratpack-1.4/​javaagent/​src/​errorContextTest/​java/​io/​opentelemetry/​javaagent/​instrumentation/​ratpack/​v1_4/​server/​RatpackErrorContextTest.java | Tests error attribution and callback parenting. | | instrumentation/​ratpack/​ratpack-1.4/​javaagent/​build.gradle.kts | Shares regression tests and adds disabled-controller variants. |
Review effort: Balanced

[Javaagent] This registry entry also changes outbound HTTP span parenting on Ratpack 1.7+. `OpenTelemetryHttpClient` selects `Execution.current().maybeGet(Context.class)` before `Context.current()` (lines 35–36). With controller telemetry disabled, a request intercepted while an application child span is current now uses the registered server context instead, making the client span a sibling of that child span. Store the error target in a dedicated registry holder and update the error lookup, or adjust client parent selection to preserve active descendant contexts. Add a regression test for an outbound request inside an application child span with controller telemetry disabled.

Ratpack errors can lose exception reporting when controller telemetry is disabled. This registers the channel-derived request context even when no handler span starts, independently of the signal-selection changes in #20648.

- **Context ownership:** Preserve handler-span error targets when enabled. Omit the current-context fallback: supported callbacks retain the request registry, while thread-current context may belong to another request.
- **Coverage:** Add disabled-controller JVM variants alongside existing enabled suites, covering synchronous, blocking, overlapping async, and forked errors, including request attribution, route naming, and callback parentage.
metadata.title: Fix Ratpack error reporting when no handler span starts
